initial:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production transparent sprite atlas for the PenguinPal desktop pet.
Input images: reference 1 = exact right-facing PenguinPal identity, outfit, illustration style and proportions; reference 2 = exact left-facing identity. These are reference poses, not the required new gait. Redraw ONLY the walk cycle while faithfully preserving the mascot: short black bob, gray-blue eyes, cyan/silver headset with microphone, rounded dark gray penguin hood with white eye circles and yellow beak, white belly panel and cyan chest badge, short flipper arms, two separate yellow penguin foot boots. NO human long legs.
Create ONE high-resolution square 2048x2048 transparent PNG atlas, perfectly regular 4 columns x 4 rows. 16 equal cells, full body centered with ample transparent gutters. Every cell has the same camera, scale, head/body proportion and floor baseline. The character stays fixed in place; no walking across the cell. No text, numbers, labels, grid, background, ground shadow or extra objects.
Read cells left-to-right then top-to-bottom. The FIRST EIGHT cells (top two rows) are ONE complete 8-phase walking-to-the-RIGHT cycle in the three-quarter side angle of reference 1. The LAST EIGHT cells (bottom two rows) are the corresponding complete walking-to-the-LEFT cycle using reference 2.
CRITICAL animation correction: the near yellow foot and far yellow foot must alternate taking a full step. Both feet must be distinctly visible and remain separate, with the far foot naturally slightly darker from occlusion, not a different color. Do NOT repeat the same forward foot in phases 0 and 4. Phase 4 must exchange which foot is forward versus phase 0.
For each eight-cell direction:
0 CONTACT A: near foot extended FORWARD toward travel direction and landing flat at the floor, far foot extended BACK touching the floor.
1 DOWN A: near forward foot supports weight; rear far heel rises preparing to lift.
2 PASS A: near foot planted under body; FAR foot lifted clearly OFF THE FLOOR passing forward beside it.
3 UP A: near foot reaches rear toe-off; FAR foot lifted and extended forward preparing to land.
4 CONTACT B: FAR foot extended FORWARD and landing at floor, near foot extended BACK touching floor. This is visibly the OPPOSITE FOOT arrangement to phase 0.
5 DOWN B: far forward foot supports weight; near rear heel rises.
6 PASS B: far foot planted under body; NEAR foot lifted clearly OFF THE FLOOR passing forward beside it.
7 UP B: far foot rear toe-off; NEAR foot lifted and extended forward preparing to return to phase 0.
For the LEFT-facing cycle mirror the travel-direction semantics while preserving the referenced character design. Use a modest visible left-right stride, subtle vertical body bob (no jumps), and small opposite flipper swings. All eight poses must advance the gait, not alternate two nearly identical stills. Head/face stay consistent and calm, neither turn to camera nor change expression. Clean crisp anime chibi painted linework exactly like reference. Genuine alpha transparency across the entire atlas, no matte.
opposite:
Use case: identity-preserve. Edit the referenced transparent PenguinPal pose to create ONE single corrected opposite walking contact pose, NOT a sheet and NOT a duplicate of the reference. Keep the identical head, face, headset, penguin hood, torso, badge, proportions and three-quarter view looking RIGHT. Transparent PNG, full body centered 256-scale subject in a large square with padding.
Only change legs, feet and small flipper swings. The reference has its LARGE NEAR yellow foot at the RIGHT/FRONT and its SMALL FAR yellow foot at LEFT/BACK. You MUST SWAP THEM:
The LARGE NEAR yellow foot must now extend clearly to SCREEN LEFT, behind the torso, planted on the ground at left of the hip; the SMALL FAR yellow foot must now extend to SCREEN RIGHT, ahead of the hip, planted on the ground at right.
Show BOTH separate feet, connected to their correct sides of the body by short penguin boot legs. The large near/back foot is in front of the belly outline at its rear corner and may show its heel. The small far/front foot is partially behind the belly but clearly protrudes to the right. The two feet have the same yellow costume design, with the far foot naturally a little darker. Keep penguin stump proportions, not human bare legs.
Make this a true opposite-leg step to the reference. DO NOT leave the larger yellow foot at screen right again. Do not simply rotate or tilt the existing right/front shoe. Both feet on the same horizontal floor baseline. A modest stride about one shoe length each side of the body. The camera-facing flipper swings gently forward (screen right), opposite the near foot stepping backward. No motion blur. The torso remains stable. Preserve original illustration identity and clean line art. No text, no arrows, no ground, no background, genuine alpha transparency.
atlas:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create a production WALK CYCLE SPRITE ATLAS for the exact transparent PenguinPal character in the three input references.
Reference 1 is RIGHT-facing contact A (large camera-near yellow foot FORWARD at screen RIGHT; smaller far foot BACK at screen LEFT).
Reference 2 is RIGHT-facing contact B (large camera-near yellow foot BACK at screen LEFT; smaller darker far foot FORWARD at screen RIGHT). Reference 2 demonstrates the ESSENTIAL opposite step. Follow its feet placement for contact B.
Reference 3 is the original LEFT-facing identity and viewing angle.
One transparent PNG, 2048x1024 landscape, EXACTLY FOUR equal columns and TWO equal rows, clean large transparent gutters, one full-body mascot per cell. NO labels/text/numbers/grid/background/ground/shadows. Same identity, head shape, face, headset and penguin costume as the references; identical scale and fixed head/body position across all 8 cells, same floor baseline. Fixed in place, not moving across a cell.
TOP ROW four poses all face RIGHT:
cell 0 CONTACT A, copy the LEG arrangement of reference 1: LARGE NEAR foot to RIGHT/front, SMALL FAR foot to LEFT/back, both grounded.
cell 1 PASS A: near leg supports body, LARGE NEAR foot grounded directly under torso, while SMALL FAR foot is CLEARLY LIFTED from ground, knee slightly bent, swinging toward screen RIGHT beside the supporting foot.
cell 2 CONTACT B, copy the LEG arrangement of reference 2: LARGE NEAR foot to LEFT/back, SMALL FAR foot to RIGHT/front, both grounded. This must be the opposite leg step to cell 0. The near boot is larger and brighter, the far boot naturally smaller and slightly darker. Do NOT put the large near boot at front/right in this cell.
cell 3 PASS B: SMALL FAR foot grounded directly under torso; LARGE NEAR foot clearly LIFTED off ground and swinging toward screen RIGHT, ready for cell 0. This exchanges which foot is lifting compared with cell 1.
BOTTOM ROW same four anatomical phases facing LEFT: cell0 near boot to LEFT/front, far boot RIGHT/back; cell1 near supports and far boot lifts toward LEFT; cell2 near boot RIGHT/back and far boot LEFT/front; cell3 far supports and near boot lifts toward LEFT.
Both feet always visible and connected to correct short penguin boot legs, no human bare legs, no extra feet, no both-feet jump, no same-foot hopping. The ground-contact foot stays on the common floor baseline and the swinging boot visibly clears it. Small opposite flipper swings, calm expression, same upper body, extremely subtle body bob. Four correctly alternating clear key poses per direction, intended to be interpolated into a smooth cycle. This must be a walking gait, not two repeated almost-identical illustrations. Crisp illustration matching the original, no blur. True transparent alpha.
passingEdit:
Use case: precise-object-edit. This is a 4-column x 2-row transparent walk-cycle atlas. Keep all eight characters, the grid layout, exact identity, scale, face, upper body and clothing unchanged. Edit ONLY the yellow feet in COLUMN TWO (the second cell in EACH row). Do not edit column one, three or four.
Purpose: column two must show the SMALL FAR FOOT lifting while the LARGE NEAR FOOT is supporting; column four already shows the LARGE NEAR FOOT lifting. The two passing poses must look different.
TOP ROW, second cell (facing RIGHT): the boot lifted forward at SCREEN RIGHT must be the FAR boot: make it visibly SMALLER, narrower and naturally DARKER GOLD, consistent with the SMALL DARK FAR FRONT BOOT in the top row THIRD cell. Raise its sole clearly above the floor, keep a short dark costume-leg connection behind the belly. The boot planted at SCREEN LEFT under the hip is the NEAR boot: make this supporting boot LARGER and BRIGHT YELLOW, clearly planted flat, consistent with the LARGE BRIGHT NEAR BOOT in the third cell.
BOTTOM ROW second cell (facing LEFT): same anatomical edit reversed horizontally. The raised boot at SCREEN LEFT is the smaller, darker golden FAR boot; the boot grounded under the hip at SCREEN RIGHT is the larger bright NEAR boot.
No added feet, no long legs, no detached feet. Both feet visible in both edited cells, one grounded, the other lifted. Keep all upper bodies and the other six cells exactly unchanged. Crisp linework, no motion blur. True transparent background, preserve alpha, no labels, no arrows, no text.
